characters: Two girls and a boy in school uniforms clapping and jumping in a playground in turns.

narrationPlan.voice: Lively voice with clear clap beats
narrationPlan.pace: Fast and rhythmic, then slower for the last verse (about 70 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: A clapping rhythm only, with no instruments (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Ampe is a clapping and jumping game played by children in Ghana. Rules and chants differ from place to place. This rhyme is original and does not set out the rules of ampe.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Ask a teacher or parent to confirm that the movements are close to the game as children play it where you are.

teacherGuide.overview: A clapping and jumping rhyme. Form: four couplets. Rhyming pairs: three/free, in/begin, mine/fine, play/day. It teaches counting, turn-taking and fair play.
learningGoals: Be a good winner and loser.
beforeReading: Ask children which clapping games they know.
whileReading: Clap on each beat. Take care that children have space.
afterReading: Play in pairs or small groups on a safe flat surface.
discussion: How do we know whose turn it is?
reflection: How do you feel when you lose a game?

support: Clap together before adding the jump.
stretch: Make up a new clapping chant.

culturalNotes: Ampe is a clapping and jumping game played by children in Ghana. Rules and chants differ from place to place. This rhyme is original and does not set out the rules of ampe.
localiseThis: Invite children to teach the real game and its chants as they know them.
